title: Finite evaluation respects the specified reduction/pullback comparison
statement: Let f be a morphism of small sites with its canonical algebraic lift, A a commutative Noetherian ring, I an ideal, K in the source derived category, and n ≥ 0. Use the strict quotient reduction/pullback isomorphism, evaluation/pullback isomorphism, finite evaluation isomorphism, scalar-restriction/pullback isomorphism, and finite scalar-extension/pullback isomorphism with the normalizations of [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison]. Evaluating the inverse of the strict reduction/pullback isomorphism and then applying the three finite target comparisons equals finite evaluation of f* K followed by restriction of the finite scalar-extension/pullback comparison. This is equality of the prescribed maps, with their finite quotient actions.

proof.text: For module inverse image, the normalized tensor insertion along the constant-ring isomorphism is invertible and natural, by scalar extension along a ring isomorphism. The normalization of the ordinary reduction/pullback comparison gives the finite module unit compatibility. Restriction along the quotient is fully faithful; use local surjectivity of the quotient and the scalar adjunction to identify the ordinary finite comparison with the evaluated tower comparison.

Apply this ordinary identity in every degree of a flat-term K-flat complex P. Pullback preserves K-flatness and flat terms; identify monoidal flatness with site flatness by the sheaf tensor comparison. Retain the iterated complex functors explicitly, using the proved complex-square hom formula and the degreewise identity of finite quotient evaluation.

Use the factorization law for derived squares of exact functors. Insert the normalized reduction, finite reduction and finite evaluation comparisons. Prove a generic pasting identity with the complex and derived functors, their factorization isomorphisms, six comparison squares, and their universally quantified normalization laws as parameters. Thus all functors remain abstract during the calculation. Naturality moves the K-flat comparison maps to a common invertible postcomposition; the ordinary degreewise identity identifies both paths, so cancel that postcomposition. Instantiate this identity for the site morphism, then transport to every derived K by a K-flat realization isomorphism and naturality.

from.place: Finite evaluation respects the specified reduction/pullback comparison

lean.statement:
theorem reductionPullFiniteEvaluation {V U : Site.{u}} (f : Morphism V U)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (K : V.derived A) (n : ℕ) :
    (U.evaluate A n).map ((f.reductionPullIso A I).inv.app K) ≫
        (f.evaluatePullIso A n).hom.app ((V.reduction A I).obj K) ≫
        (f.pull A).map ((V.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app K) ≫
        (f.finiteRestrictionPullIso A I n).hom.app ((V.finiteReduction A I n).obj K) =
      (U.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app ((f.pull A).obj K) ≫
        (U.finiteRestriction A I n).map ((f.finitePullIso A I n).hom.app K)
